info.title: Chaching API
info.description: Chaching is a modern subscription-billing platform designed to simplify product management, customer lifecycle workflows, and recurring payments. It combines a clean dashboard for business users with a powerful API built for developers who need full automation and control.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: This object represents a customer of your business. Use it to create recurring charges, save payment and contact information, and track payments that belong to the same customer.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Products describe the specific goods or services you offer to your customers. For example, you might offer a Standard and Premium version of your goods or service; each version would be a separate Product.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: Transactions represent the payments and charges made by your customers.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description: Invoices are statements of amounts owed by a customer, and are either generated one-off, or generated periodically from a subscription.

tags.name: TaxRates
tags.description: TaxRates allow you to calculate the tax to collect from your customer.

tags.name: Prices
tags.description: This object represents a price in your Chaching account. Use it to define the cost of your products, configure one-time or recurring billing intervals, specify tax behavior, and manage pricing updates or deactivations for your offerings.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description: Subscriptions are a way to charge your customers on a recurring basis. They can be used for products or services that are delivered over time, such as memberships or software licenses.

tags.name: Balance
tags.description: Balances represent the amount of money in your account. You can use balances to track your income and expenses, and to make payments to your customers or vendors.

tags.name: Payment Methods
tags.description: Payment Methods represent a way to collect payment from your customers. They can be attached to customers to make charging easier and more efficient.

tags.name: Revenue Recovery
tags.description: Revenue recovery settings control what happens when a customer's automatic payments fail: the retry schedule, what happens to the customer's subscriptions after the last retry fails, and what happens to their unpaid invoices. The settings apply to your whole account — every subscription and every payment plan — and there are no per-customer settings. Saved settings also apply to customers who already have unpaid invoices.

tags.name: Payment Plans
tags.description: Payment Plans let a customer pay off a total amount in fixed installments charged automatically to a card on file. A plan created without a payment method collects its deposit (the down payment, or installment 1 when there is none) on a registered Dejavoo terminal and stores that card for the remaining installments. This surface is gated per account and is off by default — contact Chaching to enable it.

tags.name: Dejavoo Terminals
tags.description: Dejavoo Terminals are the physical Dejavoo payment terminals of your account, each addressed by its own TPN and driven over SPIn. Register a terminal with its TPN and its 10-character SPIn Auth Key; Chaching checks the pair with SPIn before saving it. The Auth Key is write-only: it is never returned. Terminals are disabled, never deleted.

tags.name: Webhook Endpoints
tags.description: Webhook endpoints are the URLs of your server that receive ChaChing events. Every event is sent to every active endpoint of the account, signed with the account secret API key. An account holds at most 16 endpoints.

tags.name: Email Settings
tags.description: Email settings control the automatic emails ChaChing sends to your customers: payment plan receipts, failed-payment notices and overdue notices, and whether your account owner is copied on them. Both are on by default. When you turn customer emails off, you take over the card-network obligations those emails meet: a receipt for every installment and a written notice after a declined payment. Webhooks are sent either way.
